logline: A high-school girl who masters makeup to hide her insecurities finds that two boys see her for exactly who she is - and the secret she is hiding becomes impossible to keep.

renewal.note: Single-season series; concluded February 4, 2021. Named Best Korean Drama of 2021 by Forbes. No sequel produced.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 7.9, Forbes Best K-Drama of 2021, but critics and more demanding audience segments noted the webtoon's visual humour translates less cleanly than its emotional core - and the love triangle's resolution was divisive.

pull_quotes.text: True Beauty is an easy charm offensive - it asks little of the viewer and delivers steady comfort in return.

seasons.review_body: True Beauty delivers the high-school romance it promises and not very much more, which for a section of its audience is exactly enough. Moon Ka-young's Jugyeong is a sympathetic protagonist whose anxiety about appearance reads as genuinely felt rather than manufactured, and Cha Eun-woo's visual charisma does the work the plot sometimes does not. The show earned Forbes' Best Korean Drama of 2021 designation, which reflects its popularity rather than its formal ambition. The webtoon's broader commentary on beauty standards - sharper on the page - arrives in the drama as a gentle undercurrent rather than a central argument. Hwang In-youp as the second male lead became the season's breakout figure, as the show acknowledged by giving his character a more coherent arc than the romance logic strictly required. Viki audiences and Rotten Tomatoes audience scores ran higher than IMDb's 7.9 suggests; critics were notably quiet, which is itself a reading.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: True Beauty Season 1 Episode 1 aired December 9, 2020 on tvN as the series premiere. The series holds a 7.9 IMDb rating and was named Forbes' Best Korean Drama of 2021. The RT consensus called it 'an easy charm offensive - it asks little of the viewer and delivers steady comfort in return.' The premiere delivers precisely that: Jugyeong's backstory - bullying, the makeup transformation, the new school identity - is established efficiently and with enough empathy for the protagonist's anxiety to feel genuine. Moon Ka-young's physical comedy lands immediately; Cha Eun-woo's visual charisma carries the first encounter with Lee Su-ho in the webtoon's genre register without irony. The premiere's most effective quality is its refusal to apologise for being what it is: a comfort-watch romance with a likeable protagonist, stage-managed with the proficiency of a Studio Dragon production that has already assessed its audience.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes Jugyeong's world - the bullying backstory, the makeup transformation, and the new school identity - with enough pace to keep the genre audience engaged. The first encounter with Lee Su-ho is staged with the webtoon's visual language intact.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Jugyeong's first day at the new school without her mask on - the vulnerability that drives the season lands here.

critic_note.text: A likeable lead and confident visual grammar make True Beauty an easy recommendation for genre fans.
